n01-open
Not every architecture starts as a sentence. <break time='200ms'/> Some start on a whiteboard. <break time='200ms'/> Others are already running in Azure.
n02-title
This episode: from a sketch, or from what's already deployed, to an editable Azure diagram.
n03-photo
Here's a whiteboard from a design session: real-time messaging, drawn in generic terms. <break time='150ms'/> There isn't a single Azure service name on it.
n04-upload
Drop the photo into Generate Diagram. AADB reads the boxes, the arrows and the labels, <break time='100ms'/> even the messy handwriting.
n05-gen
Then it maps every box to the Azure service that does that job, and keeps the flows between them.
n06-tour
The WebSocket gateway, the message broker, the in-memory store, the push notifications: <break time='120ms'/> each one is now a real Azure service, grouped and connected.
n07-ref
And the original sketch stays pinned to the canvas, so anyone can check the translation.
n08-import
Already running in Azure? <break time='150ms'/> Import it instead.
n09-options
Bring a Bicep, Terraform or ARM template, <break time='120ms'/> or reverse-engineer a live resource group straight from Azure: read-only, with your own permissions.
n10-arm
Here's an exported resource group with fourteen resources. <break time='120ms'/> In under a second, they're on the canvas: grouped, priced and connected.
n11-edges
And every connection says what the reference actually means: <break time='100ms'/> runs in, pulls images from, reads secrets from, sends messages to. <break time='150ms'/> Nothing is guessed.
n12-yours
From there, it's your diagram. Drag services and groups into the layout that tells the story best.
n13-close
A whiteboard photo, a template, or a live resource group: <break time='150ms'/> every path leads to the same editable, priced Azure diagram.
